I could not fix this, and the restatement below is a resubmission of attempt 2, unchanged. Both failures report `unexpected token '³'` at line 4. Attempt 2 contains no `ℝ³`, so the error appears to come from the original statement copied verbatim, which uses the file's `local notation "ℝ³"`. That notation seems not to be in scope when the theorem is assembled, and nothing on the restated side can change that. I have not verified this reading.

The restatement itself pushes the negation inside the existential, using Mathlib's `not_exists`. The proof is a single `simp only [not_exists]` that should close the iff.

```json
{"mode":"iff","restated":"∃ (u₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic u₀ ∧ ForceConditionPeriodic f ∧ ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ → ℝ), ¬ NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic nu u₀ f v p","proof":"simp only [not_exists]","english":"For every viscosity nu > 0 there exist smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic initial data u₀ and a smooth, 1-periodic, time-decaying force f on the 3-torus, such that for every candidate velocity v and pressure p, the pair (v, p) is not a smooth periodic solution of Navier–Stokes with data (u₀, f).","why_clearer":"It replaces the negated existential over (v, p) with a universal statement that no pair is a solution, and writes the space as EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) instead of the local ℝ³ notation."}
```

parsed.english: For every viscosity nu > 0 there exist smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic initial data u₀ and a smooth, 1-periodic, time-decaying force f on the 3-torus, such that for every candidate velocity v and pressure p, the pair (v, p) is not a smooth periodic solution of Navier–Stokes with data (u₀, f).
